exposition: Understand that standard, factored, and vertex forms expose different features of one function. Name the changing and fixed quantities, define any reference value or input interval, and decide what would count as a plausible result. An estimate, sign prediction, graph feature, or domain statement made before calculation becomes an independent check afterward. Consider the worked problem: Rewrite f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 in factored and vertex form, then name the feature exposed by each form. Skipping the middle line may hide the exact sign, factor, interval, or restriction on which the conclusion depends.
